distinguishing_features: Passive floating clamp ring converts a pressure differential into additional seal preload
Annular chamber behind the ring is supplied with ambient subsea pressure through a restriction orifice
Radial lip seal is reloaded as the ring translates under the ambient-to-internal pressure difference
Mechanism targets post-creep restoration of sealing contact stress rather than leak detection or operating-limit reduction
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Maintain sufficient sealing contact stress in a subsea hydraulic connector after pressure and thermal cycling causes elastomeric creep and stress relaxation, without adding a powered actuator.
parsed.viable_reason: The proposed force balance is not physically credible as written because typical internal hydraulic pressure can exceed ambient pressure, cooling does not necessarily reduce internal pressure, and the described axial translation of an annular ring is not shown to produce the required radial lip-seal compression or verified 10% preload recovery.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the cited prior art suggests a passive pressure-actuated floating-ring mechanism for mechanically reloading a connector seal, so that specific mechanism would not be an obvious application of the closest cited approaches.
